# Methodology
GDP measures annual output; gross capital formation measures annual fixed investment and inventory changes. Gross fixed capital formation excludes inventory changes. Maintain consistent definitions across the series.

For starting GDP S, target T and n years, nominal US-dollar CAGR=(T/S)^(1/n)-1. GDP at k=S*(1+CAGR)^k. Investment share at k=b+(r-b)*k/n. Comparison investment=GDP*b; scenario investment=GDP*share. Sum k=1..n for cumulative flows.

The same GDP path is used for the comparison and scenario. The comparison is conditional, not a financing commitment. Differences are not measured external financing gaps. Do not infer causal growth from investment ratios. Separate real GDP, GDP deflator and FX; use investment efficiency only as a labelled sensitivity.

## Reconciliation
Map funded transactions to new productive domestic assets. Exclude financial asset trades and refinancing from new capital formation unless associated qualifying investment is identified. Separate ultimate funding sources from intermediaries. Count a pension-held bank-financed bond only once. Guarantees are not funded capital. Track commitments, disbursements and operating outcomes separately. Do not equate FDI flows with gross capital formation without adjustment.

## Baseline adoption
Retrieve source series; preserve raw responses and timestamps; identify calendar vs fiscal years, revisions, currency, price basis and null values; independently reproduce historical averages; reconcile country statistics with WDI. Document discrepancies before publication.
